target_customer: Landlords, real estate investors, property managers and proptech platforms that embed insurance
problem: Investment property insurance is slow, opaque and handled through agents who undersell the specialist product. Landlords wanted fast online quotes and coverage.
business_model: Insurance agency and MGA earning commission and premiums; embedded distribution through partners

founders.name: Ryan Letzeiser
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (May 2021) says the brothers have backgrounds in insurance and real estate private equity, without saying who has which.

founders.name: Aaron Letzeiser
founders.background_notes: Brother of Ryan; both listed as founders on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Quoting and binding software plus carrier and regulatory integration across states. Standard engineering with licensing as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: State licences, carrier relationships and embedded partner integrations (more than 75 proptech partners by 2023) are slow to copy, though the underlying product is plain insurance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Battery Ventures said in 2021 there were very few digital competitors; incumbents did not copy it, and Baldwin bought it in January 2026.

market_need_then: Landlord insurance is a specialised, nuanced product with few digital sellers; Obie reported premiums rising from about $1M in its first year to about $10M a year later.

branding.domain_note: Moved from obierisk.com to obieinsurance.com (Coverager headline Obierisk.com is now ObieInsurance.com); date not confirmed.

identity.logo: Paper airplane after the April 2025 rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: Forward-looking, tagline Moving Investment Property Insurance Forward

branding.brand_signature: Paper airplane symbol of forward momentum

rebrands.to: New brand centered on a paper airplane
rebrands.why: Symbolize forward momentum and progress, per CEO quote

brand_strength.rationale: Short friendly name and a deliberate 2025 rebrand, but no evidence of community, merch or press about the brand beyond the rebrand release.

pivots.why: Team saw a gap in investment property insurance, per Built In and Accelerant coverage; date approximate

outcome_analysis: Obie pivoted from landlord asset management into landlord insurance, raised a $10.7M Series A in May 2021 and a $25.5M Series B in May 2023 (about $39M total equity), and grew into embedded distribution through proptech partners. The Baldwin Group completed its acquisition in January 2026 at an undisclosed price, a plausible strategic exit for a niche distribution platform with few digital rivals.
notes: No competitor source dated near 2019 was found. Founder education and prior employers not found in opened sources. Series B investor list is from search snippets of the company release; the page itself was not opened. Series A lead is Battery per TechCrunch, ZoomInfo says Second Century (not used). Obie reportedly acquired Skylight Insurance in 2020 per a search snippet, not verified. Press release and fintechfutures launch page returned 403 and were not worked around. The Baldwin deal page was seen only via search results. Seed or pre-Series A funding not found.
